Les 5 jeunes de la cohorte 2023-2024 de: The five young people in the 2023-2024 cohort of the École Converse Podcast.
De novembre 2023 à mars 2024, cinq jeune: From November 2023 to March 2024, five young Montrealers from various neighbourhoods took part in the 2024 École Converse Podcast, in collaboration with <l1>la Puce à l'oreille</l1>. Kester, Nesim, Sadjida, Sami and Adrianna, who range in age from 16 to 19, represent both geographic and ethnic diversity. Despite their different backgrounds and origins, they share one thing: the desire to shed light on the reality of young people from the neighbourhoods, which is often trivialized.
« On n’est pas importants, parce qu’on h: “We don’t matter, because we live way out on the edge of Montréal, because we come from a bad neighbourhood, because we’re Black, because we’re Arab,” Kester says bluntly. “Just ’cause you’re Arab doesn’t mean you’re gonna end up a thug!” Sami exclaims.
Originaires de différents quartiers de M: Coming from different parts of Montréal, including Rivière-des-Prairies, Laval, Saint-Michel and Saint-Léonard, the young people discover over the weeks that they share similar concerns, particularly social ills. Their common experiences extend beyond the boundaries of their respective neighbourhoods.
Le fruit de leur collaboration, intitulé: The fruit of their collaboration, titled “Pas Tout Montréal,” exposes the reality of young people from the neighbourhoods, caught between stigmatization and the desire to make their voices heard.
Ces jeunes incarnent la résilience et l’: These young people embody resilience and hope. Beyond the struggles of their daily lives, they share their aspirations for a better future. By claiming their place in society, they are the spokespeople of a generation determined to make its voice heard.
Interrogés sur la nature du mal social,: Asked about the nature of social ills, the École Converse students concisely describe their shared experience: “A social ill is a sick society whose symptoms we suffer. It’s not just a social difficulty, but an ongoing problem. It’s an injustice, a rejection, a situation that persists day after day,” Kester sums up.
Pour illustrer cette idée, Sami offre un: To illustrate the idea, Sami offers a concrete example: “One of my Algerian friends, when he came to Canada at five, had trouble speaking and making friends. That’s a social difficulty. But years later, in high school, he was still being rejected. He started feeling alone because he was being discriminated against; and that’s a social ill.”
Sadjida partage une perspective similair: Sadjida shares a similar perspective, pointing out that social ills often stem from one community being valued over another. In her neighbourhood, she sees racialized people being rejected, even though they are the majority. She cites examples such as a soccer field being converted into a baseball diamond, a sport that is far less popular among the neighbourhood’s residents. Sami adds that there is a general indifference toward North Africans in his own neighbourhood.
« Au départ, on ne pensait pas partager: “At first, we didn’t think we shared the same social ills, but we ended up realizing that our experiences were similar,” Sami explains.
Réunis par leurs luttes quotidiennes con: Brought together by their daily struggles against social rejection, stigmatization, racism and police violence, each of these young people lives with a social ill. Perhaps you’ll recognize yourself in one of their stories.
Kester, qui a 18 ans, réside à Rivière-d: Kester, 18, lives in Rivière-des-Prairies. A podcast fan for a few years now, he jumped at the chance when a community worker in his neighbourhood told him about École Converse. The young man sees it as a springboard. For him, it’s an opportunity to learn to put words to what he experiences every day, he tells us.
Prenant la parole pour se présenter, il: Introducing himself, he describes himself as a young man who doesn’t particularly shine at school and is often bored in class, but who is bursting with creativity. Throughout the podcast, Kester presents himself with spontaneity and a touch of humour, captivating listeners with his endearing personality and quick wit.
En prenant la parole, le jeune homme veu: By speaking up, the young man wants to highlight the glaring differences that can exist between Montréal’s sought-after neighbourhoods and Montréal-Nord. “In the west of Montréal, people know what goes on in Montréal-Nord, but they don’t really know what goes on.” According to him, “not all of Montréal is safe.”
Témoin de plusieurs incidents où des arm: Having witnessed several incidents involving weapons, Kester often comes home from school with a knot of fear in his stomach. “It affects my mental health,” he admits.
« Je veux que les gens sachent, je veux: “I want people to know, I want them to become aware of our realities. There’s a side of Montréal that doesn’t get media coverage,” he says. “They don’t know what it feels like to be left behind,” Kester adds. “In Rivière-des-Prairies… it’s empty, empty, empty,” he repeats, to drive home the isolation he feels in his neighbourhood.
Tout au long du balado, Kester partage s: Throughout the podcast, Kester shares his observations and anecdotes, offering a unique perspective on the reality of his neighbourhood and challenging the stereotypes often associated with Montréal-Nord.

Nesim, âgé de 16 ans, réside à Saint-Mic: Nesim, 16, lives in Saint-Michel. The young man exudes a calm confidence. His voice is measured, almost professorial, reflecting a maturity beyond his years. A Saint-Michel native, Nesim is involved in his neighbourhood with the Forum Jeunesse. In fact, it was through a coordinator at the organization that he heard about École Converse.
Son engagement a commencé dès l’âge de 1: His involvement began at the age of 14 with Jeunesse Implique, an organization he founded himself.
Nesim n’a pas toujours fait preuve de la: Nesim hasn’t always shown the determination that drives him today. In the first episode of “Pas Tout Montréal,” he humbly admits that when he was younger, he wasn’t a particularly studious student. However, an experience with a teacher that he describes as racist left a deep mark on him, even becoming a real turning point in his life. This traumatic experience was a catalyst for him and pushed him to redouble his efforts to break stereotypes, not only for himself but also for his community.
Nesim est conscient des barrières social: Nesim is aware of the social barriers he faces as a young person of North African origin. “In Montréal, Arabs are often associated with violence and disruption,” he remarks. “Not all young Montrealers have to push themselves to break stereotypes,” he says a few moments later. Nesim nevertheless refuses to be reduced to his origins. His approach is clear: “I’m a young Arab, but I’m also just a young person, or a young person who’s involved and engaged.”
Il nourrit des aspirations élevées pour: He has high aspirations for the future. He wants to study law and then move into the health field. His goal is to “keep improving and progressing,” both academically and in terms of social engagement.

Sadjida, qui a 16 ans, vit à Saint-Léona: Sadjida, 16, lives in Saint-Léonard. When asked what “Pas Tout Montréal” means to her, she replies: “Not all of Montréal has to make an effort to be accepted.”
Sadjida est une jeune fille d’origine ma: Sadjida is a young woman of North African origin who wears the hijab. She says she feels torn between rejection and pride in being different. “The fact that people talk to me differently, that they treat me differently because of my origins or my hijab, that can hurt me,” she confides. “When I walk down the street, my hijab draws attention, and what I see in other people’s eyes is discomfort.”
Douce de nature, Sadjida donne l’impress: Gentle by nature, Sadjida comes across as shy at first, but you only need to scratch the surface to discover the strength and depth of her thoughts. Despite her young age, she draws attention and commands admiration, from people her own age as well as older ones. She describes herself as a flower, evoking her delicacy, but at the same time she aspires to become a strong woman, able to overcome obstacles and defend her convictions with courage.
La jeune femme a conscience que son iden: The young woman is aware that her identity, her personality and even her most personal aspirations are often called into question by other people’s preconceived judgments. “People don’t have enough faith in my aspirations, maybe because in their view, Arabs are doomed to a certain type of job,” she suggests.
Du haut de ses 16 ans, Sadjidja réalise: At just 16, Sadjida is already realizing some of her professional dreams. Hoping to devote her life to writing, she is currently working on a novel about young people facing inescapable hardships. The author wants to give young people hope again. “Even if we’re in a pretty tough spot, we can get out of it if we ask ourselves the right questions,” she says.
La jeune femme a plus d’un tour dans son: The young woman has more than one trick up her sleeve. Since she was 14, she has been building a custom-order pastry business alongside her studies. But her real passion is journalism, she tells us. For her, this podcast is an opportunity to discover the profession.
Sami, âgé de 16 ans, habite à Laval. Il: Sami, 16, lives in Laval. In École Converse, he found an opportunity to get involved with racialized youth and to examine the experiences of racism and social abandonment lived by some young people.
D’origine algérienne, Sami a subi du rac: Of Algerian origin, Sami has experienced racism. Yet he considers himself privileged. “Sure, I’ve experienced racism, but not as much as others, because I was born here,” he says. The young man is referring in particular to the experience of his friends who were born abroad. “My immigrant friends experienced racism as soon as they arrived and they’re constantly rejected. Nobody wants to hang out with them.”
Résidant du quartier Duvernay, à Laval,: A resident of the Duvernay neighbourhood in Laval, Sami often witnesses the social isolation some young people face. “A bit further from my place, I see people hanging around together, young people who’ve been socially rejected, and that has dangerous consequences,” he remarks. He is aware that young people are not treated equally. “Not all of Montréal gets considered,” he asserts.
Attaché à sa communauté, Sami aspire à d: Deeply attached to his community, Sami hopes to one day be a source of help for future generations. “If I succeed and make it to the top, I’m not gonna turn my back. I know where I come from. I’ll be able to help others, because I’ll have lived what they’re living,” he tells us.
Pour les années à venir, Sami envisage u: In the years ahead, Sami is considering an artistic career, particularly in rap.

Adrianna, qui a 19 ans, habite à Rivière: Adrianna, 19, lives in Rivière-des-Prairies. She is the oldest in the group. It was La Converse’s reputation that made her want to join École Converse. “My values connect with La Converse. There’s a real message being communicated,” she says, snapping her fingers.
The young woman is good with her hands. A self-employed marketing consultant, Adrianna helps local companies and racialized-owned businesses grow their social media. On top of that, she also works part-time as an esthetician.
Ce parcours entrepreneurial n’est pas un: This entrepreneurial path isn’t one she expected to take so soon. A studious young woman, Adrianna was deeply shaken in 2022 when an alert forced the evacuation of Cégep Maisonneuve due to the possible presence of a firearm on the school’s premises.
Plongée dans cette situation, Adrianne s: Caught up in the situation, Adrianna found herself facing police officers’ guns. This traumatic experience, which she says was “tinged with racism,” led her to make a difficult decision: to drop out of school, as the school environment had become a source of anxiety for her. “It’s sad, because this wasn’t the academic path I’d planned for myself,” she confides with a mix of regret and resolve. However, despite not having a diploma, she remains clear-eyed and hopeful about her future, convinced that her journey won’t end there.
Résidente de Rivière-des-Prairies, Adria: As a resident of Rivière-des-Prairies, Adrianna faces the same realities as Kester, even though she is a woman. “It’s part of life, well, my life… I’m aware that not everyone lives the same realities,” she points out.
Fille d’un intervenant social, la jeune: The daughter of a social worker, the young woman reflects on her surroundings and doesn’t hesitate to express her opinions. In La Converse’s studio, she dives without hesitation into a frank discussion about the normalization of the violence racialized people face, while opening her heart to share her own dreams and aspirations.
Pour l’avenir, Adrianna souhaite explore: For the future, Adrianna wants to explore several other fields. “I like doing a lot of things, honestly. But what I’m really passionate about is film.”
Dans le dernier épisode du balado, les é: In the podcast’s final episode, the students open up and take the time to write a letter to the person they will become in a few years. They have a message for those who oppressed them, for those who supported them and for those who share their reality.
Sadjida se lance : « Je voudrais dire à: Sadjida goes first: “I’d like to say to the person who’s like me and who’s listening to me: you are not alone. We just have to have hope and work.”
Nesim s’adresse à lui-même et aux audite: Nesim speaks to himself and to listeners: “If you’ve made it to that level, it’s because you deserve it. You should be proud of yourself!”
